card: This pull request adds an optional sat_vb boolean parameter to getmempoolinfo, getnetworkinfo, estimatesmartfee, and estimaterawfee, returning fee rates in sat/vB rather than BTC/kvB. It addresses user friction and downstream calculation bugs stemming from client-side conversion of legacy BTC/kvB units, especially in sub-1 sat/vB scenarios. Fee rate serialization is handled by a new ValueFromFeeRate helper providing 3 decimal places of precision. The work implements part of issue #32093 and has no prerequisites.
changed_since_previous: The underlying approach and affected RPCs remain unchanged from the previous description.
evidence: PR description references issue #32093, stating: 'Returning feerates in BTC/kvB it can be very burdensome and is not good practice, as the most widely adopted units are sat/vB.'

PR description highlights sub-1 sat/vB rounding problems: 'Because of sub 1sat/vB environment we cannot rely on GetFee() because it internally uses FeeFrac EvaluateFee() function which rounds the values to always return an int. If the feerate < 1 then it will be rounded to 1 or 0.'
problem: Bitcoin Core RPCs return fee rates denominated in BTC/kvB, while users and downstream applications standardly work with sat/vB. Callers must convert units manually, which introduces friction and can cause rounding errors, particularly in sub-1 sat/vB conditions where naive integer conversions round to zero or one.

risk.why: Modifying positional RPC parameter layouts or fee rate formatting outputs could break existing client applications relying on exact argument indexes or values.

scope_notes: Although the PR description mentions modifying `getwalletinfo`, that RPC is not touched in this diff. Reviewers should note that adding `sat_vb` as a positional parameter to `estimatesmartfee` shifts the `options` argument from index 2 to index 3.
summary: Adds an optional boolean argument `sat_vb` to `getmempoolinfo`, `getnetworkinfo`, `estimatesmartfee`, and `estimaterawfee` RPCs. When enabled, returned fee rates are represented in sat/vB instead of the default BTC/kvB. It implements a `ValueFromFeeRate` helper in `core_io` to format fee rates with 3 decimal digits of precision without relying on integer rounding.
